patients.summary: Young man who joined the practice healthy in 2021 and developed paranoid schizophrenia in 2022: an oculogyric crisis on haloperidol, two failed second-generation trials, then clozapine from 2023. In 2025 TMP-SMX given at urgent care was followed by febrile neutropenia with agranulocytosis; clozapine was rechallenged and briefly interrupted again for an ANC of 800 in late 2025.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - PREVENTIVE

25 y/o M here to set up primary care. No PCP since his pediatrician aged him out. Now on MassHealth. Full-time student at a college about forty minutes away, commutes, and picks up part-time shifts at a warehouse in town on weekends. Lives with his father in Greenfield.

No complaints today. Sleeps fine, eats fine.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: father has schizophrenia. Maternal aunt with bipolar disorder. No known early heart disease, diabetes or cancer in first-degree relatives.
Social: never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs including cannabis. Drives. Seatbelt always.
Immunizations: childhood series per state registry printout. COVID primary series (Pfizer x2) done this spring per registry. Last Td-containing vaccine in middle school.

ROS: negative x12 systems.

Exam: vitals reviewed in flowsheet. Well appearing, pleasant, good eye contact, organized speech. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Neuro grossly intact, gait normal. Mood good, affect bright.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P: healthy 25M.
- Tdap today (over ten years). Flu shot today.
- One-time HIV and hep C screens sent.
- Discussed family psychiatric history in general terms; he knows his father's illness well. Told him the door is open if sleep, mood or thinking ever feels off.
- RTC 1 yr for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Miles, your HIV and hepatitis C screening tests came back negative (nonreactive). Nothing else to do there. Good to meet you on Tuesday.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 05/24/2022

CC: "he's not himself" (per father)

25M accompanied by father. Over a period of months has pulled away from friends and stopped attending classes; he has left college. He says classmates were talking about him and that he was being recorded by cameras hidden in the house. Father reports he stays in his bedroom with the door locked and can be heard talking for hours with no one there. Showering rarely, has stopped helping around the house and no longer joins in family conversation. Father has watched him murmur and gesture as though replying to a voice.

Pt denies alcohol, cannabis or other drug use.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: VS within normal limits. Alert. Responds in brief phrases after long latency. Flat, detached. Denies thoughts of harming himself or anyone else. No focal neuro deficit.

No grounds for involuntary hold; father comfortable taking him home.

Impression: first-episode psychosis; presentation consistent with schizophrenia, paranoid type.

Disposition: discharged home with father. Urgent outpatient psychiatry intake arranged. Return for any danger to self or others. Follow up with PCP.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Phone Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Father (on pt's release, verbal OK from pt on the line) calling after son was seen in the ED Tues for paranoid thinking. ED note in chart. Psych intake is set for 6/13, father wants to know if Dr can see him before then. Pt quiet on the call but agreeable. No safety concerns voiced, father says he is eating and sleeping some. Booked Wed 6/1 at 2:40 with PCP. ED precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here with his father after ED eval 5/24 (record reviewed). Miles answers in a word or two, often after a long pause. Acknowledges he left school this spring. When asked about the cameras he says "I don't want to talk about that here." Denies wanting to hurt himself or anyone. Sleeping irregularly. Eating less. No substance use, confirmed again alone with him. No headache, fever, seizures, head injury.
Father is worried but calm, knows the illness from his own history.

Meds: none. NKDA.

O: vitals in flowsheet. Hygiene fair. Guarded, flat. Thought process slow. Not obviously responding to internal stimuli in the room. Neuro nonfocal, normal gait, no tremor or rigidity.

A/P: first-episode psychosis, dx per ED schizophrenia, paranoid type.
- Psychiatry intake 6/13 confirmed. Gave father the crisis line and when to go back to the ED.
- Baseline labs before antipsychotic treatment: CBC w diff, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH.
- Release signed so we can talk with father.
- See me after psychiatry has met him, ~6 wks.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 06/20/2022

CC: stiff neck, eyes rolling up

25M, seen here about four weeks ago for new psychotic symptoms. Two hours ago developed a stiff, pulling neck and his eyes locked upward. Psychiatry started haloperidol at a clinic visit one week ago (6/13). No fever, no head injury, no other new meds.

Meds: haloperidol 5 mg qhs.
Allergies: none known prior to today.

Exam: VS normal. Eyes held in upward gaze, intermittently. Sustained contraction of the neck muscles with twisting, repetitive movements and intermittent fixed abnormal posture. Mentating at baseline per father. No meningismus once dystonia relieved.

Tx: diphenhydramine 50 mg IV x1 at 18:20. Eye deviation and neck posturing resolved by 19:05. Observed 2 h, no recurrence.

Impression: acute dystonic reaction / oculogyric crisis due to haloperidol.

Disposition: home. STOP haloperidol. Haloperidol entered as intolerance (oculogyric crisis/acute dystonia). Psychiatry to see him this week to choose another agent. Return if symptoms recur.

Allergies at discharge: haloperidol (oculogyric crisis/acute dystonia).

documents.title: Phone Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called after reading the 6/20 ED record. Spoke with Miles and then father. No further stiffness or eye symptoms since the IV dose. He has not taken any haloperidol since. Psych appt Friday 6/24. Haloperidol added to allergy list as intolerance. Told them a repeat episode means ED again.

documents.title: Phone Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Father LVM then reached on callback. Psychiatry saw Miles Fri 6/24 and started aripiprazole 10 mg once a day. Took first doses over the weekend, no stiffness. Med list updated (outside Rx). Father asks that we keep him in the loop, release on file.

Meds: aripiprazole 10 mg daily (outside). Intolerance: haloperidol.

A/P
1. Schizophrenia, paranoid type - psychiatry managing. Tolerating aripiprazole.
2. Oculogyric crisis 6/20 from haloperidol - resolved, intolerance listed.
Weight/A1c/lipids again in a few months for antipsychotic monitoring. RTC fall, flu shot then.

reports.text:
CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST
Clinical indication: psychosis, altered orientation.
Technique: axial images from skull base to vertex without IV contrast.
Findings: The lateral ventricles are enlarged. Third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No extra-axial collection. Basal cisterns patent. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells clear. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged lateral ventricles. No acute intracranial abnormality.

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 05/19/2023

CC: brought in by roommate for strange behavior

26M with paranoid schizophrenia, first episode about a year ago, also had an oculogyric crisis on haloperidol last June. Roommate says for roughly six months he has retreated from everyone, is heard talking to himself in his room, and now insists outside forces are steering his thoughts. Currently prescribed olanzapine by outpatient psychiatry.

Allergies: haloperidol (oculogyric crisis/acute dystonia).

Exam: unkempt, poor eye contact, appears to be attending to internal stimuli. Oriented to self only; does not know where he is or the date. Neuro exam without deficit: CN intact, strength and sensation symmetric, no abnormal movements.

Data: urine tox screen negative. Non-contrast CT head: enlarged lateral ventricles, nothing acute (report attached).

Impression: acute exacerbation of paranoid schizophrenia.

Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (300 mg) by mouth at bedtime

Admit 05/19/2023  Discharge 06/09/2023

Dx: schizophrenia, paranoid type, treatment-resistant (failed aripiprazole and olanzapine trials).

NEW: clozapine 300 mg PO at bedtime (started 5/23, titrated). ANC monitoring weekly through outpatient psychiatry lab.
NEW: docusate sodium 100 mg PO daily.
STOPPED: olanzapine 15 mg (tapered off 6/2).

Allergies: haloperidol (oculogyric crisis/acute dystonia).

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry 6/13. PCP within 1-2 weeks.

Post-discharge visit. Inpatient psych 5/19-6/9 after the ED visit his roommate brought him to (ED record and CT reviewed; discharge med list reviewed).

S: Feels "clearer." Voices are less. Back at the apartment with his roommate, father checking in daily. Saw psychiatry yesterday, CBC drawn there, weekly from here on. Taking clozapine 300 mg at night and docusate every morning. Bowels moving daily. No fever, sore throat. No SI.

Meds: clozapine 300 mg qhs (psychiatry), docusate 100 mg daily. Olanzapine stopped.
Allergy/intolerance: haloperidol - oculogyric crisis.

O: vitals in flowsheet; weight up about 3 kg since last summer. Calm, more eye contact than last year, organized enough to give his own history. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, normal BS. No abnormal movements.

A/P
1. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia, paranoid type - now on clozapine via psychiatry, who own ANC monitoring. Asked them to cc us on results.
2. Antipsychotic metabolic monitoring: weight gain on olanzapine. A1c and lipids today. Discussed food and activity.
3. Head CT ventricular enlargement noted in ED report.
RTC ~5 months.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - MEDICINE
Admitted 05/22/2025 via ED. Discharged 05/28/2025.

Diagnoses: febrile neutropenia; drug-induced agranulocytosis, attributed to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
History: treatment-resistant schizophrenia on clozapine; oculogyric crisis with haloperidol (2022).

Presentation: 28M with 3 days of high fevers, marked fatigue and painful sores in his mouth. Was seen at an urgent care on 5/12 for a skin abscess and given TMP-SMX DS twice daily x7 days, completed. T 38.9 C in the ED. Ulcers along the gum line and inside both cheeks. WBC 1.4, ANC 0.1 (100/mm3); hemoglobin and platelets normal.

Course: blood cultures drawn, then empiric cefepime IV. Neutropenic precautions. Clozapine held as a possible contributor; psychiatry aware, restart decision deferred to outpatient psychiatry. Afebrile from hospital day 3. Blood cultures no growth at 5 days. Oral lesions improving. ANC 1.6, WBC 3.4 morning of discharge.

Allergies updated: trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (agranulocytosis) - avoid. Haloperidol (oculogyric crisis/acute dystonia).

Discharge meds: docusate 100 mg daily. HOLD clozapine until cleared by psychiatry.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC with differential. Psychiatry next week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call, discharge summary in chart. Pt at home, no fever since the hospital, mouth less sore, eating soft foods. Has not taken clozapine since admission, understands to hold it until psychiatry says otherwise. Sulfa antibiotic added to allergy list, he knows to tell any provider. Appt Mon 6/2 with CBC. Fever 38.0 or higher before then = ED.

conditions.label: Drug-induced agranulocytosis
conditions.note: Counts recovered; TMP-SMX listed as allergy

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit - Post Hospital
documents.author: PCP

Hospital f/u. Admitted 5/22-5/28 with febrile neutropenia / agranulocytosis after TMP-SMX given at urgent care for a skin abscess (discharge summary reviewed). I didn't know about the urgent care visit at the time.

S: Feels much better. No fevers at home. Mouth sores nearly gone, eating normally. Energy coming back. Off clozapine since 5/22. Psychiatry appt Thursday 6/5. No SI.

Meds: docusate 100 mg daily. Clozapine on hold.
Allergies: TMP-SMX (agranulocytosis); haloperidol (oculogyric crisis).

O: vitals in flowsheet, afebrile. Mouth: a few healing shallow spots on the buccal mucosa, gums otherwise normal. No cervical nodes. Skin: abscess site healed. Heart/lungs normal.

CBC with diff today: WBC and ANC back in the normal range; result will be faxed to psychiatry today.

A/P
1. Febrile neutropenia / agranulocytosis - resolved. TMP-SMX allergy entered (high criticality).
2. Schizophrenia - clozapine restart is psychiatry's call; they have today's CBC.
Call with any fever.
